Umeda · Nakazakichō · Tenma · Tenjinbashi-suji · Nakanoshima · Fukushima

  1. Must see · Kita

    Umeda Sky Building — Kuchū Teien Floating Garden Observatory

    The 173 m twin-tower skyscraper (1993) joined at the top by the open-air Floating Garden observation deck — 360° views over Osaka, open till 22:30.

    Look for observation deck

    Umeda Sky Building, northwest of JR Osaka Station, Kita-ku, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by japan-guide.com — Osaka, Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), Wikipedia

  2. Must see · Kita

    LUCUA Characters World — Pokémon Center Osaka & Nintendo OSAKA

    Osaka's answer to Tokyo's Character Street: LUCUA SOUTH opened 5 April 2026 and gathered Pokémon Center Osaka, Nintendo OSAKA and the ONE PIECE Mugiwara Store (moved from Daimaru Umeda) on its top floors, growing to 30+ character shops (Sanrio, Square Enix, Minecraft) by autumn 2026.

    Look for ★ Anime & pop culture — Pokémon · Nintendo (Mario, Zelda, Splatoon) · One Piece — Kansai's biggest official character-store cluster, the Pokémon Center and Nintendo flagship stores of western Japan · character shops, pop culture

    LUCUA SOUTH 10–13F (South Gate Building), JR Osaka Station, Umeda, Kita-ku, Osaka

    Recommended by japan-guide.com — Osaka, Time Out Osaka, Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau)

  3. Must see · Michelin & Fine Dining · Kita

    Yoshiko

    One Michelin star (2026); second-generation fugu chef in Kitashinchi, wife a certified sake advisor — Osaka is one of Japan's biggest fugu-eating cities.

    1-8-5 Sonezakishinchi, Kita-ku, Osaka 530-0002

    Recommended by Michelin ★, Michelin Editorial

  4. Must see · Kaiseki, Kyō-ryōri & Ryōtei · Kita

    Oimatsu Hisano

    Michelin Two Stars (2026) Japanese restaurant; chef-owner Masamitsu Hisano sources the finest seasonal produce from across Japan.

    4-8-3 Nishitemma, Kita-ku, Osaka 530-0047, Japan

    Recommended by Michelin ★

  5. Must see · Kaiseki, Kyō-ryōri & Ryōtei · Kita

    Recommended by Michelin ★

  6. Must see · Michelin & Fine Dining · Kita

    Tosara

    One MICHELIN Star contemporary restaurant; Agu pork and Awaji lettuce from the chef's parents' farm, served shabu-shabu style, is one of the inspectors' favourite dishes.

    2-7-26 Nishitemma, Kita-ku, Osaka 530-0047, Japan

    Recommended by Michelin ★

  7. Worth the detour · Kita

    Nakanoshima Museum of Art, Osaka

    The city art museum that opened on Nakanoshima in February 2022 — modern and contemporary art and design, part of the island's museum cluster.

    Look for art museum

    Nakanoshima, Kita-ku, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), japan-guide.com — Osaka, Wikipedia

  8. Worth the detour · Kita

    Osaka City Central Public Hall (Nakanoshima)

    Neo-Renaissance red-brick hall completed 1918 with a donation from stockbroker Einosuke Iwamoto (design Tatsuno Kingo & Okada Shin'ichirō); restored 1999–2002 and designated an Important Cultural Property in 2002. Free basement history exhibit.

    Look for historic architecture

    Nakanoshima, Kita-ku, Osaka

    Recommended by Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), Wikipedia, Time Out Osaka

  9. Worth the detour · Kita

    Tsuyu no Tenjinsha (Ohatsu Tenjin)

    1,300-year-old Umeda shrine named for Sugawara no Michizane's dew-and-tears poem; nicknamed after Ohatsu, heroine of Chikamatsu's 1703 'Love Suicides at Sonezaki', set in its grove — now a matchmaking power spot.

    Look for shrine

    Sonezaki, Kita-ku, Osaka

    Recommended by Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), Time Out Osaka, Wikipedia

  10. Worth the detour · Kita

    Osaka Tenmangū

    Temma's shrine to Sugawara no Michizane, god of learning, at the head of Tenjinbashi-suji; home of the Tenjin Matsuri.

    Look for shrine

    Temma, Kita-ku, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), Wikipedia

  11. Worth the detour · Kita

    Japan Mint (Osaka) — cherry-blossom passage

    The national mint where Japan's coins are struck; famous for opening its riverside avenue of cherry trees to the public each spring.

    Look for mint, sakura

    Temma, Kita-ku, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), Wikipedia

  12. Worth the detour · Kita

    National Museum of Art, Osaka

    Contemporary Japanese and international art on two underground floors of Nakanoshima; the 2007 building's entrance structure is designed to evoke growing bamboo.

    Look for art museum

    Nakanoshima, Kita-ku, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by japan-guide.com — Osaka, Wikipedia

  13. Worth the detour · Kita

    Tenjinbashi-suji Shopping Street

    Claimed as Japan's longest covered shopping street — 2.6 km of shops and eateries running north from the Tenmangū approach.

    Look for shopping arcade

    Tenjinbashi 1-7 chōme, Kita-ku, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), japan-guide.com — Osaka

  14. Worth the detour · Kita

    Kitashinchi

    Osaka's grown-up entertainment quarter just south of Osaka Station — hundreds of restaurants, hostess bars and counters.

    Look for dining & nightlife district

    Sonezakishinchi, Kita-ku, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by japan-guide.com — Osaka, Wikipedia

  15. Worth the detour · Kita

    Nakazakichō

    A pocket of pre-war row houses east of Umeda whose narrow lanes are now full of cafés, craft shops and vintage stores.

    Look for retro neighbourhood

    Nakazakinishi, Kita-ku, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by japan-guide.com — Osaka, Wikipedia

  16. Worth the detour · Kita

    Grand Green Osaka & Umekita Park

    The Umekita redevelopment beside JR Osaka Station — a large urban park with new towers opening in stages through spring 2027, next to the Grand Front Osaka complex.

    Look for urban park

    Ōfukachō, Kita-ku, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by japan-guide.com — Osaka, Wikipedia

  17. Worth the detour · Kita

    Osaka Museum of Housing and Living (大阪くらしの今昔館)

    Walk-through, life-size reconstruction of an Edo-period Osaka merchant townscape on the upper floors of a building at the north end of Tenjinbashi-suji. Closed for renovation until 5 January 2027 (japan-guide e4024) — check before visiting.

    Look for museum

    Tenjinbashi 6-chōme, Kita-ku, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), Wikipedia

  18. Worth the detour · Kita

    Temma Tenjin Hanjo Tei (天満天神繁昌亭, rakugo theatre)

    Osaka's dedicated rakugo hall (yose) beside Osaka Tenmangū — the home stage of Kamigata comic storytelling, with daily shows.

    Look for theatre

    Tenjinbashi 2-chōme, Kita-ku, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), Wikipedia

    Capcom's third store and first Kansai café (opened Nov 2022) — ~900 Monster Hunter / Resident Evil / Street Fighter goods plus a 56-seat rotating collab café; still trading in 2026 (Ōkami 20th-anniversary collab, June 2026) after the building's 13F became LUCUA SOUTH.

    Look for ★ Anime & pop culture — Capcom (Monster Hunter, Resident Evil, Street Fighter, Ōkami) — the publisher's only Kansai store-café, Osaka being Capcom's home city · game store & collab café

Minami 55

Namba · Dōtonbori · Shinsaibashi · Amerikamura · Kuromon · Sennichimae · Ura-Namba

  1. Must see · Minami

    Mandarake Grand Chaos (Nipponbashi)

    Six floors of manga, anime, retro games, idol merch, cosplay and collectibles, vintage to new; Mandarake's Osaka flagship relocated from Amerikamura to Den Den Town in December 2020.

    Look for ★ Anime & pop culture — Mandarake — Osaka's flagship used-otaku megastore, the anchor of Den Den Town · shop

    4-12-6 Nipponbashi, Naniwa-ku, Osaka

    Recommended by Osaka Metro NiNE (metronine.osaka), Osaka Metro NiNE (metronine.osaka), Inside Osaka, Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), Wikipedia

  2. Must see · Minami

    Dōtonbori

    The canal-side heart of kuidaore Osaka: neon, mechanised signs (the Glico Running Man, the Kani Doraku crab) and street food that barely closes.

    Look for nightlife, street food

    Dōtonbori, Chuo-ku, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by japan-guide.com — Osaka, Time Out Osaka, Wikipedia

  3. Must see · Minami

    Hōzen-ji & Hōzenji Yokochō

    A moss-covered Fudō Myōō statue that worshippers splash with water, beside two 80 m stone-paved alleys of old kappo counters, bars and okonomiyaki shops — the setting of Oda Sakunosuke's 'Meoto Zenzai'.

    Look for temple, lantern-lit alleys

    Namba, Chuo-ku, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by japan-guide.com — Osaka, Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), Wikipedia

  4. Must see · Teishoku, Curry & Yōshoku · Minami

    Hokkyokusei Shinsaibashi Honten

    Western-style restaurant founded 1922 where omurice was invented in 1925; the main shop occupies a former tea house with tatami rooms and a garden in Nishi-Shinsaibashi.

    2-7-27 Nishi-Shinsaibashi, Chuo-ku, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), Time Out Osaka, Inside Osaka

  5. Must see · Minami

    Kuromon Market

    "Osaka's Kitchen": a several-hundred-metre covered arcade of fishmongers, butchers, greengrocers and grill-it-on-the-spot stalls.

    Look for market

    Nipponbashi, Chuo-ku, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by japan-guide.com — Osaka, Time Out Osaka

  6. Must see · Minami

    Ebisubashi & the Glico Running Man sign

    The bridge over the Dōtonbori canal where everyone poses with the Glico Running Man — the neon heart of Minami's mechanised signs.

    Look for neon sign, bridge

    Ebisubashi bridge, Dōtonbori, Chuo-ku, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by japan-guide.com — Osaka, Wikipedia

  7. Must see · International & Fusion · Minami

    551 Hōrai Honten (Namba)

    Osaka's most renowned butaman maker — the steamed pork bun every domestic traveller carries home; this is the Namba main store of the city-wide chain.

    3-6-3 Namba, Chuo-ku, Osaka 542-0076, Japan

    Recommended by Time Out Osaka, Wikipedia

  8. Must see · Kissaten & Coffee · Minami

    Pokémon Center Osaka DX & Pokémon Café

    Western Japan's only permanent Pokémon Café (opened 20 Sept 2019 with the DX store): Pikachu curry, Eevee pancakes and Pokéball desserts, reservation-only; reopened June 2026 after a renewal.

    Look for ★ Anime & pop culture — Pokémon — the Pokémon Company's own café and DX-format store, one of only two Pokémon Cafés in Japan

    Daimaru Shinsaibashi Main Bldg 9F, 1-7-1 Shinsaibashi-suji, Chuo-ku, Osaka 〒542-8501

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Time Out Osaka

  9. Must see · Michelin & Fine Dining · Minami

    Kani Doraku Dōtonbori Honten (かに道楽 道頓堀本店)

    The Osaka-born crab house whose giant moving 3D crab sign is one of Dōtonbori's iconic photo spots (Time Out); the honten serves crab course menus.

    Dōtonbori 1-6-18, Chūō-ku, Osaka

    Recommended by Time Out Osaka, Wikipedia

  10. Must see · Wagyu, Yakiniku & Sukiyaki · Minami

    Harijyu Dōtonbori Honten (はり重)

    A century-old Dōtonbori beef house: Time Out calls it legendary for melt-in-the-mouth wagyu sukiyaki and shabu-shabu; ja.wikipedia documents the honten.

    〒542-0071 Dōtonbori 1-9-17, Chūō-ku, Osaka

    Recommended by Time Out Osaka, Wikipedia

  11. Must see · Wagashi, Matcha & Sweets · Minami

    Rikuro Ojisan no Mise Namba Honten (りくろーおじさんの店)

    Osaka's beloved fluffy raisin-bottomed cheesecake, branded with the uncle's face and baked to order (OSAKA-INFO, Dec 2025); the Namba shop is the company's honten (ja.wikipedia).

    Namba, Chūō-ku, Osaka

    Recommended by Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), Wikipedia

  12. Must see · Izakaya, Yakitori & Yokochō · Minami

    Takoume Honten (たこ梅 本店)

    Founded in 1844 and billed as Japan's oldest oden restaurant, now run by the fifth generation; the counter serves kanto-daki oden, the signature saezuri (whale tongue) and sweet-simmered octopus, and was a haunt of writers Oda Sakunosuke and Kaikō Takeshi (Time Out Osaka; GLT/JTB Publishing).

    Dōtonbori, Chuo-ku, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by Time Out Osaka, Good Luck Trip (gltjp.com)

  13. Must see · Ramen & Tsukemen · Minami

    Naniwa Menjiro (なにわ 麺次郎)

    Michelin Guide-listed ramen counter inside Kintetsu Osaka-Namba Station and a Tabelog Ramen OSAKA Hyakumeiten 2025 pick; the clam-dashi Ōgonkai ramen is the signature, with Oigatsuo ramen as runner-up.

    4-1-17 Namba, Chūō-ku, Osaka 542-0076 (inside Kintetsu Osaka-Namba Station — platform ticket needed)

    Recommended by Michelin Guide Japan — Osaka region selection, Tabelog Hyakumeiten

  14. Must see · Kaiseki, Kyō-ryōri & Ryōtei · Minami

    Taian

    Three MICHELIN Stars (2026): 'Taian' means 'big hut' — modest, clean décor, with Japanese cuisine that crystallises the skill and passion of Hitoshi Takahata.

    1-21-2 Shimanochi, Chuo-ku, Osaka 542-0082, Japan

    Recommended by Michelin ★

  15. Must see · International & Fusion · Minami

    milpa

    One MICHELIN Star: the first Mexican restaurant in Japan to earn a star, a four-table room in Kita-Horie cooking Indigenous Mexican ingredients and techniques in a modern way.

    1-16-25 Kitahorie, Nishi-ku, Osaka 550-0014, Japan

    Recommended by Michelin ★

  16. Worth the detour · Minami

    Daimaru Shinsaibashi Main Building (大丸心斎橋店 本館, Vories)

    William Merrell Vories' 1933 neo-Gothic department store on Midōsuji; rebuilt 2019 reusing the original tiled façade, peacock relief and Art Deco interiors — Lmaga runs Vories architecture walks here and OSAKA-INFO lists it as a historic-architecture highlight.

    Look for architecture / department store

    Shinsaibashi-suji 1-chōme, Chūō-ku, Osaka

    Recommended by Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), Lmaga.jp (京阪神エルマガジン社), Wikipedia

  17. Worth the detour · Minami

    Shinsaibashi PARCO Character Floors (Chiikawa Land · Donguri Republic)

    Shinsaibashi PARCO's 'POP CULTURE SHINSAIBASHI' floors gather character flagships with photo spots — Chiikawa Land (creator Nagano's official shop, 6F), a large Donguri Republic Ghibli store, Kiddy Land and more; directly linked to Shinsaibashi Station.

    Look for ★ Anime & pop culture — Chiikawa & Studio Ghibli — Osaka's character-shop floor (Chiikawa Land, Donguri Republic) · shop

    Shinsaibashi PARCO 5F–6F, 1-8-3 Shinsaibashi-suji, Chuo-ku, Osaka

    Recommended by Lmaga.jp (京阪神エルマガジン社), Lmaga.jp (京阪神エルマガジン社), Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), Walkerplus / Kansai Walker (kadokawa)

  18. Worth the detour · Soba & Udon · Minami

    Dotonbori Imai

    Udon house founded in 1946 in the middle of the Dōtonbori strip — one of Osaka's most famous noodle specialists, serene inside, known for its dashi and kitsune udon.

    Dōtonbori, Chuo-ku, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), Inside Osaka, Lonely Planet — Osaka

  19. Worth the detour · Okonomiyaki, Takoyaki & Kushikatsu · Minami

    Okonomiyaki Fukutaro Sennichimae Honten (福太郎)

    Old-school Sennichimae okonomiyaki house cooking to order; its signboard dish is the suji negiyaki, beef strips and negi in a fluffy batter. Named by Time Out Osaka and Inside Osaka among Namba's okonomiyaki standbys and profiled by Savor Japan.

    2-3-17 Sennichimae, Chuo-ku, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by Time Out Osaka, Inside Osaka, Savor Japan

  20. Worth the detour · Minami

    Shinsaibashi-suji Shopping Arcade

    Osaka's premier shopping street — a ~600 m covered arcade mixing chain stores, boutiques and department stores, running north from Dōtonbori.

    Look for shopping arcade

    Shinsaibashi-suji, Chuo-ku, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by japan-guide.com — Osaka, Wikipedia

  21. Worth the detour · Minami

    Amerikamura (Amemura)

    Osaka's answer to Harajuku: thrift stores, cafes and youth fashion around Triangle Park, west of Mido-suji.

    Look for youth culture, shopping

    Nishishinsaibashi, Chuo-ku, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by japan-guide.com — Osaka, Wikipedia

  22. Worth the detour · Minami

    Den Den Town (Nipponbashi)

    Osaka's Akihabara: electronics, anime, games and maid cafés along Sakaisuji in Nipponbashi.

    Look for ★ Anime & pop culture — Kansai's otaku district — Nipponbashi Ota Road, Animate, Mandarake and Jungle for anime, manga, figures and retro games · electronics & otaku district

    Nipponbashi, Naniwa-ku, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), Wikipedia

  23. Worth the detour · Minami

    National Bunraku Theatre

    The nation's most prestigious stage for bunraku, Osaka's own puppet theatre — runs of about three weeks in January, April, June, July/August and November.

    Look for puppet theatre

    Nipponbashi, Chuo-ku, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by japan-guide.com — Osaka, Wikipedia

  24. Worth the detour · Minami

    Namba Yasaka Shrine

    Famous for its 12 m-high lion-head stage, whose gaping mouth swallows bad luck and brings victory in competition; the shrine was rebuilt after the 1945 air raids and keeps an intangible-folk-culture tug-of-war rite.

    Look for shrine

    Motomachi, Naniwa-ku, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), Wikipedia

  25. Worth the detour · Minami

    Namba Grand Kagetsu (NGK)

    Yoshimoto's 858-seat 'hall of laughter', Japan's largest comedy theatre — Yoshimoto Shinkigeki, manzai and rakugo 365 days a year.

    Look for comedy theatre

    Namba-sennichimae, Chuo-ku, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), Wikipedia

  26. Worth the detour · Minami

    Animate Osaka Nipponbashi

    One of western Japan's largest official anime/manga goods stores, the Ota Road anchor; the same building holds Lashinbang, Melonbooks and card-game floors.

    Look for ★ Anime & pop culture — Animate — the official anime-goods chain's big Osaka store on Ota Road · shop

    Nipponbashi-nishi, Naniwa-ku, Osaka (Den Den Town)

    Recommended by Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), Inside Osaka

  27. Worth the detour · Minami

    Jump Shop Osaka Shinsaibashi

    Weekly Shōnen Jump's official shop (One Piece, Dragon Ball, Demon Slayer, Jujutsu Kaisen merch) on Daimaru Shinsaibashi's 9th-floor pop-culture zone beside Pokémon Center Osaka DX.

    Look for ★ Anime & pop culture — Weekly Shōnen Jump — the magazine's official store (One Piece, Dragon Ball, JJK) · shop

    Daimaru Shinsaibashi 9F, Shinsaibashi-suji, Chuo-ku, Osaka

    Recommended by Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), Walkerplus / Kansai Walker (kadokawa)

  28. Worth the detour · Minami

    Kōzu-gū (高津宮, Kōzu Shrine)

    Hilltop shrine to Emperor Nintoku, founded by imperial decree in 866 at the reputed site of the Naniwa Takatsu Palace and moved here when Hideyoshi built Osaka Castle; famous as the setting of classic rakugo stories, with rakugo still performed in the grounds. Rebuilt after WWII air raids (one Edo-period storehouse survived).

    Look for shrine

    1-1-29 Kōzu, Chūō-ku, Osaka

    Recommended by Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), Wikipedia

  29. Worth the detour · Kissaten & Coffee · Minami

    Kirby Café Osaka

    The third permanent Kirby Café (opened 21 Nov 2024) with Osaka-only dishes — a Waddle Dee okonomiyaki burger, kushikatsu in an Inhaling Kirby bowl, takoyaki-style petit cakes; reservations sell out months ahead.

    Look for ★ Anime & pop culture — Kirby (Nintendo / HAL Laboratory) — official permanent Kirby Café with an Osaka-exclusive kuidaore menu

    Daimaru Shinsaibashi 9F, 1-7-1 Shinsaibashi-suji, Chuo-ku, Osaka

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Siliconera

  30. Worth the detour · Kissaten & Coffee · Minami

    Kissaten founded by Sadao Ibuki in 1934 (Imaike), main store in Sennichimae since 1946 — an Osaka institution for dark-roast drip coffee whose regulars included Kasagi Shizuko and Shofukutei Shokaku.

    1-9-1 Sennichimae, Chuo-ku, Osaka 542-0074, Japan

    Recommended by Time Out Osaka, Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau)

    Dōtonbori, Chuo-ku, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by Inside Osaka, Good Luck Trip (gltjp.com)

  32. Worth the detour · Okonomiyaki, Takoyaki & Kushikatsu · Minami

    Ajinoya Honten (味乃家)

    Near-seventy-year-old okonomiyaki specialist by the Dōtonbori arcade, known for a cabbage-heavy, light batter; order the Ajinoya Mix (pork, squid, octopus, shrimp) or the negiyaki (Inside Osaka; GLT/JTB Publishing).

    2F, 1-7-16 Namba, Chuo-ku, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by Inside Osaka, Good Luck Trip (gltjp.com)

  33. Worth the detour · Okonomiyaki, Takoyaki & Kushikatsu · Minami

    Okonomiyaki Yukari Sennichimae (ゆかり 千日前店)

    Sennichimae branch of the Osaka okonomiyaki house credited with handing down the 'mixed' Osaka style; recommended in OSAKA-INFO's Japan Konamon Association konamon guide and in SAVOR JAPAN's 15 best okonomiyaki in Osaka.

    Recommended by Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), Savor Japan

  34. Worth the detour · Okonomiyaki, Takoyaki & Kushikatsu · Minami

    Hōzenji Yokochō Yakizen (法善寺横丁 やき然)

    Okonomiyaki counter inside the stone-paved Hōzenji Yokochō alley; Rurubu's spot page highlights its blended flour, secret sauce and Hōzenji-yaki, and Mapple lists it among Minami's 17 okonomiyaki picks for its fluffy batter and suji negiyaki.

    1-1-18 Namba, Chūō-ku, Osaka

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ, JTB Publishing), Mapple / まっぷるウェブ (Shobunsha Publications)

    Okonomiyaki Okaru (お好み焼 おかる, Sennichimae)

    Shōwa-era Sennichimae okonomiyaki house of some 70 years, famous for the okami drawing Tsūtenkaku, Billiken or celebrities in mayonnaise on each pancake; in Rurubu's 12 must-eat okonomiyaki shops (Minami) and Kansai Walker's 8 popular okonomiyaki for visitors.

    Recommended by Rurubu (るるぶ, JTB Publishing), Walkerplus / Kansai Walker (kadokawa)

    Okonomiyaki Sanpei Shinsaibashi (おこのみやき 三平, Shinsaibashi-suji)

    Negiyaki specialist near Shinsaibashi known for its very tall green-onion pancakes; in Rurubu's 12 must-eat okonomiyaki shops (Minami) and Mapple's Minami/Kita okonomiyaki 17. (Separate shop from the Hōzenji Sanpei in the yokochō.)

    2-2-10 Shinsaibashi-suji, Chūō-ku, Osaka

  45. Deep cut · Minami

    The only museum anywhere with a permanent display of Kamigata (Osaka-Kyoto) ukiyo-e — realistic kabuki-actor prints of stars like Nakamura Utaemon III, ~30 works over four small floors, plus print-making classes (reservation). Free with the Osaka Amazing Pass.

    Namba 1-chōme (corner lot west of Hōzen-ji), Chūō-ku, Osaka

  46. Deep cut · Minami

  47. Deep cut · Minami

    Temple founded by Gyōki in 744; its wooden main hall (rebuilt 1808) miraculously survived the WWII air raids amid the Minami neon. Appears in Chikamatsu's Sonezaki Shinjū and the rakugo story 'Mameda'.

  55. Closed — kept for the record · Minami

    CLOSED: Dōtonbori's neo-Renaissance theatre (opened 1923 as a cinema, kabuki/stage house since 1997) gave its final performance, the 'Onagori Gogatsu Ōkabuki', on 26 May 2026 after 103 years; Shochiku plans to demolish the ageing building. Facade-only now — no shows.

Chūō & the Castle 52

Osaka Castle · Honmachi · Kitahama · Tanimachi · Karahori

  1. Must see · Chūō & the Castle

    Osaka Castle

    Hideyoshi's 1583 castle, rebuilt in 1931 — the main keep (a museum with a top-floor lookout) rises from stone walls and moats in a vast park famous for plum and cherry blossom.

    Look for castle, museum, park

    Osakajō, Chuo-ku, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by Time Out Osaka, Wikipedia

Tsūtenkaku · Shinsekai · Abeno Harukas · Shitennō-ji · Nishinari

  1. Must see · Tennōji & Shinsekai

    Shinsekai & Tsūtenkaku

    The 'New World' district built after the 1903 Expo — half Paris, half Coney Island — around Tsūtenkaku, the 103 m tower rebuilt in 1956; the home of Osaka kushikatsu.

    Look for retro district, tower

    Ebisuhigashi, Naniwa-ku, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by japan-guide.com — Osaka, Wikipedia

  2. Must see · Tennōji & Shinsekai

    Shitennō-ji

    Founded by Prince Shōtoku in 593 — one of Japan's oldest temples and the first built by the state, with its five-storey pagoda on the classic straight-line layout.

    Look for temple

    Shitennōji, Tennoji-ku, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by japan-guide.com — Osaka, Wikipedia

  3. Must see · Tennōji & Shinsekai

    Abeno Harukas 300 Observatory

    The ~300 m skyscraper that opened in 2014 — department store, hotel, art museum and the Harukas 300 observation deck with panoramic views across Osaka.

    Look for observation deck

    Abenosuji, Abeno-ku, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), Wikipedia

  4. Must see · Okonomiyaki, Takoyaki & Kushikatsu · Tennōji & Shinsekai

    Yaekatsu

    Jan Jan Yokochō's long-queue kushikatsu counter (founded post-war, 1940s), profiled by Inside Osaka and singled out by Nippon.com as the Shinsekai shop with the longest lines.

    Jan Jan Yokochō (Nan'yō-dōri), Ebisuhigashi, Naniwa-ku, Osaka

    Recommended by Inside Osaka, Inside Osaka, nippon.com (Nippon Communications Foundation)

  5. Must see · Sushi & Kaisen-don · Tennōji & Shinsekai

    Sushi Harasho

    Two MICHELIN Stars (2026 MICHELIN Guide Japan) sushi counter in Uenomiya-chō, Tennōji — the top-rated sushi on the Uemachi plateau, served as an omakase of nigiri.

    3-30 Uenomiyacho, Tennoji-ku, Osaka 543-0037, Japan

    Recommended by Michelin ★

  6. Worth the detour · Tennōji & Shinsekai

    Aizen-dō Shōman-in (愛染堂勝鬘院)

    Temple of Aizen Myōō, the deity of love and marriage, whose 1597 Hideyoshi-rebuilt tahōtō pagoda is an Important Cultural Property and the oldest wooden building in Osaka city; its Aizen Matsuri (30 Jun–2 Jul) opens Osaka's summer festival season.

    Look for temple

    5-36 Yūhigaoka-chō, Tennōji-ku, Osaka

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), Time Out Osaka

  7. Worth the detour · Tennōji & Shinsekai

    Taiyoshi Hyakuban (鯛よし百番, Tobita)

    Taishō-era former Tobita yūkaku brothel building, now a working ryōtei; its lavish interiors are a nationally Registered Tangible Cultural Property (2000) and the go-to place in Japan to step into the world of Demon Slayer's Entertainment District arc, since nothing comparable survives in Tokyo's old Yoshiwara.

    Look for ★ Anime & pop culture — Demon Slayer (Kimetsu no Yaiba) — Entertainment District (Yūkaku-hen) arc: surviving Taishō pleasure-quarter interiors featured by Mapple as the arc's real-world pilgrimage spot · historic ryōtei / former yūkaku architecture

    3-5-25 San'ō, Nishinari-ku, Osaka 557-0001

    Recommended by Mapple / まっぷるウェブ (Shobunsha Publications), Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), Wikipedia

  8. Worth the detour · Wagashi, Matcha & Sweets · Tennōji & Shinsekai

East Osaka 21

Tsuruhashi · Ikuno Koreatown · Kyōbashi · Higashi-Ōsaka

  1. Must see · East Osaka

    Ikuno Korea Town (Miyuki-dōri)

    Japan's largest Koreatown: about 150 grocers, kimchi and chijimi stalls, restaurants and hanbok shops along a 300 m shopping street in Ikuno, a short walk from Tsuruhashi's yakiniku alleys.

    Look for Koreatown, street food

    Momodani 3-chōme, Ikuno-ku, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), Wikipedia

  2. Must see · East Osaka

    Hiraoka Shrine (枚岡神社)

    Kawachi's ichinomiya at the foot of the Ikoma range, said to date back 2,600+ years; famous for its plum grove and the 23 December 'laughing ritual' (Owarai Shinji).

    Look for shrine

    7-16 Izumoi-chō, Higashi-Ōsaka, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), Wikipedia

  3. Must see · East Osaka

    Ishikiri Tsurugiya Shrine (石切劔箭神社)

    'Ishikiri-san', the god of swellings — nationally known for the ohyakudo-mairi, worshippers circling between the stones and the hall, and a fortune-teller-lined approach street.

    Look for shrine

    1-1-1 Higashi-Ishikiri-chō, Higashi-Ōsaka, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), Wikipedia

  4. Must see · East Osaka

    Fujita Museum of Art (藤田美術館)

    Meiji magnate Fujita Denzaburō's collection of ~2,000 Asian artworks — 9 National Treasures (incl. a yōhen tenmoku tea bowl) and 53 Important Cultural Properties — in a rebuilt gallery by Kyōbashi.

    Look for museum

    Amijima-chō, Miyakojima-ku, Osaka (Kyōbashi side), Japan

    Recommended by Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), Wikipedia

  5. Must see · Kaiseki, Kyō-ryōri & Ryōtei · East Osaka

    Katamachi Kawaguchi (片町 川口)

    Chef Hiroshi Kawaguchi's kaiseki counter near Kyōbashi, reopened under this name in 2023; awarded One MICHELIN Star in the Michelin Guide Kyoto Osaka 2025.

    1-3-11 Katamachi, Miyakojima-ku, Osaka 534-0025

    Recommended by Michelin ★

  6. Worth the detour · East Osaka

    Tamatsukuri Inari Shrine (玉造稲荷神社)

    An ancient shrine on the Uemachi plateau, said to date from 12 BC and long linked to the guardianship of Osaka Castle. OSAKA-INFO calls it the 'princess shrine' because all its deities are goddesses, and it draws women praying for good matches and health. It is also tied to the magatama (curved bead) craft the Tamatsukuri district is named for.

    Look for shrine

    Tamatsukuri, Chūō-ku, Osaka (5 min walk from JR Morinomiya / Metro Tamatsukuri exit 1)

    Recommended by Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), Wikipedia, Rurubu (るるぶ, JTB Publishing), OsakaMania (オオサカマニア, Osaka Metro)

    Estate office built in 1707 by the Kōnoike merchant house to run the farmland reclaimed after the Yamato River was rerouted; the main house and four storehouses were designated Important Cultural Properties in 1980, and the grounds keep a stroll garden. Rare surviving Edo-period land-development office.

    Look for historic house

    Kōnoike Motomachi, Higashi-Ōsaka, Osaka (5 min walk from JR Kōnoike-Shinden Station)

    Recommended by Agency For Cultural Affairs, Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), Wikipedia

    Recommended by Michelin Guide Japan — Osaka region selection

  19. Deep cut · Sushi & Kaisen-don · East Osaka

    Sushidokoro Hirokawa

    Michelin Guide-listed sushi counter: fish is selected at Tsuruhashi Market and the nigiri are formed small so you can sample as many items as possible.

  21. Deep cut · Izakaya, Yakitori & Yokochō · East Osaka

Bay Area 19

Universal Studios · Kaiyūkan · Tempozan · Taishō Little Okinawa · Sakishima

  1. Must see · Bay Area

    Super Nintendo World (Universal Studios Japan)

    The world's first Super Nintendo World opened inside USJ on 18 March 2021 (Mario Kart: Koopa's Challenge, Yoshi's Adventure); the Donkey Kong Country expansion (Mine Cart Madness) opened 11 Dec 2024 and grew the land by ~70%. Timed-entry via the USJ app on busy days.

    Look for ★ Anime & pop culture — Nintendo — Super Mario & Donkey Kong; the first Nintendo theme-park land anywhere, built in Osaka · theme-park land

    Universal Studios Japan, 2-1-33 Sakurajima, Konohana-ku, Osaka

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), Time Out Osaka, Inside Osaka

  2. Must see · Bay Area

    Universal Studios Japan

    Opened in 2001 as the first Universal Studios park in Asia; one of Japan's most visited theme parks, with areas including The Wizarding World of Harry Potter and Super Nintendo World.

    Look for ★ Anime & pop culture — Super Nintendo World (the world's first, 2021) — Mario Kart, Donkey Kong Country and Nintendo characters, plus Harry Potter, Minions and seasonal anime collabs · theme park

    2-1-33 Sakurajima, Konohana-ku, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by japan-guide.com — Osaka, Wikipedia, Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau)

  3. Must see · Bay Area

    Osaka Aquarium Kaiyūkan

    One of Japan's largest aquariums, built around a 5,400-ton central Pacific tank holding a whale shark, with exhibits themed on the Pacific Rim.

    Look for aquarium

    1-1-10 Kaigan-dori, Minato-ku, Osaka (Tempozan Harbor Village), Japan

    Recommended by japan-guide.com — Osaka, Wikipedia, Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau)

  4. Worth the detour · Bay Area

    Tempozan Giant Ferris Wheel

    A 112.5 m Ferris wheel beside Kaiyūkan in Tempozan Harbor Village, with a roughly 15-minute ride over Osaka Bay and the city skyline.

    Look for Ferris wheel

    Tempozan Harbor Village, 1-1-10 Kaigan-dori, Minato-ku, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by japan-guide.com — Osaka, Wikipedia, Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau)

  5. Worth the detour · Bay Area

    Sakishima Cosmo Tower Observatory

    Observation deck 252 m up atop the Sakishima building (completed 1995), giving a 360-degree panorama of Osaka Bay; known for night views.

    Look for observation deck

    Osaka Prefectural Government Sakishima Building, 1-14-16 Nanko-kita, Suminoe-ku, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), Wikipedia

  6. Worth the detour · Bay Area

    Maishima Incineration Plant (舞洲工場)

    Hundertwasser-designed waste plant on an artificial island — red, black and white walls, a golden onion tower and roof greenery; free guided interior tours by reservation.

    Look for architecture

    Maishima, Konohana-ku, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), Wikipedia

  7. Worth the detour · Bay Area

    Kyocera Dome Osaka (京セラドーム大阪)

    Look for stadium

    Chiyozaki, Nishi-ku, Osaka (by Taishō), Japan

    Recommended by Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), Wikipedia

  8. Worth the detour · Bay Area

    Osaka Nanko Bird Sanctuary (大阪南港野鳥園)

    Free tidal-flat wetland built on Sakishima as a stop-over for migratory shorebirds, with an observation building and tower; closed Wednesdays.

    Nankō-kita, Suminoe-ku, Osaka (NW corner of Sakishima)

    Recommended by japan-guide.com — Osaka, Wikipedia

    Sawashi Shoten (沢志商店, Hirao Little Okinawa)

    Okinawan grocery on Hirao's 'Little Okinawa' shopping street, backed by the Okinawan community for ~50 years; featured by Osaka's official tourism guide (Shittonka Osaka) and Walkerplus's Little Okinawa guide. Closed Mondays.

    3-15-19 Hirao, Taishō-ku, Osaka

    Recommended by Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), Walkerplus / Kansai Walker (kadokawa)

  10. Worth the detour · Sushi & Kaisen-don · Bay Area

    A Bib Gourmand in the MICHELIN Guide Japan 2026, a neighbourhood sushi counter in Nishikujō on the way to USJ.

    1-23-13 Nishikujō, Konohana-ku, Osaka 554-0012

    Recommended by Michelin Bib

  11. Deep cut · Bay Area

    Tempozan Marketplace / Naniwa Kuishinbo Yokocho

    The harbour mall at the heart of Tempozan Harbor Village, beside the Ferris wheel and Kaiyūkan; inside are the retro Shōwa food alley Naniwa Kuishinbo Yokochō and LEGOLAND Discovery Center Osaka.

    Tempozan Harbor Village, 1 Kaigan-dōri, Minato-ku, Osaka, Japan

  12. Deep cut · Bay Area

    Senbonmatsu Ōhashi — the 'Megane-bashi' loop bridge (千本松大橋)

    1,228 m road bridge (1973) built 33 m above the Kizu River so ships can pass; the two-tier spiral approaches gave it the nickname 'Megane-bashi' (spectacles bridge), and the Taishō side is a three-level loop. Osaka City lists it as a landscape resource, best seen together with the free Senbonmatsu ferry below it.

    Look for bridge / viewpoint

    over the Kizu River, linking Taishō-ku and Nishinari-ku, Osaka

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Osaka City official (city.osaka.lg.jp), Mapple / まっぷるウェブ (Shobunsha Publications)

  13. Deep cut · Bay Area

    Namihaya Ōhashi (なみはや大橋)

    1,573 m S-curved bridge (1995) over the mouth of the Shirinashi River. Its 250 m central span is Japan's largest for a girder bridge. You can walk across it in about 30 minutes, with a 360° harbour panorama that takes in the Chitose and Shin-Kizugawa bridges. Osaka City and Osaka Metro's Osaka Mania both feature it.

    Look for bridge / viewpoint

    mouth of the Shirinashi River, linking Minato-ku and Taishō-ku, Osaka

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Osaka City official (city.osaka.lg.jp), OsakaMania (オオサカマニア, Osaka Metro)

    Look for park

    Tempozan Park, Chikkō, Minato-ku, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), Wikipedia

  15. Deep cut · Bay Area

    Chikkō Red Brick Warehouse, Chikkō, Minato-ku, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), Wikipedia

It stocks cuts ordinary butchers don't carry, such as skin-on pork, chiragā and offal, all domestic pork, and its griddled horumon is a takeaway favourite. Featured by Kansai Walker's Little Okinawa guide and OSAKA-INFO's Little Okinawa article.

Southern Osaka 26

Sumiyoshi Taisha · Sakai kofun & knives · Kishiwada · Kansai Airport

  1. Must see · Southern Osaka

    Mozu Kofun Group — Daisen Kofun (Emperor Nintoku's Tomb)

    Cluster of 5th-century keyhole tombs in Sakai, UNESCO World Heritage (2019) with the Furuichi group; Daisen Kofun, attributed to Emperor Nintoku, is the largest grave in the world by area (~840 m with moats). The mound itself is off-limits.

    Look for kofun / burial mounds

    Daisen-cho, Sakai-ku, Sakai, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by japan-guide.com — Osaka, Wikipedia, UNESCO World Heritage Centre

  2. Must see · Southern Osaka

    Sumiyoshi Taisha

    Head shrine of over two thousand Sumiyoshi shrines across Japan, protecting travellers and sailors; its four main halls face west in the ancient Sumiyoshi-zukuri style.

    Look for shrine

    2-9-89 Sumiyoshi, Sumiyoshi-ku, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by japan-guide.com — Osaka, Wikipedia

  3. Must see · Southern Osaka

    Kanshin-ji (観心寺)

    Ancient Kōyasan Shingon temple (founded 701, restored by Kūkai 815) holding the National Treasure Nyoirin Kannon and Kondō hall; plum, cherry and autumn-leaf spot.

    Look for temple

    Kawachinagano, Osaka, Japan

    Recommended by Osaka-info (Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau), Wikipedia

159 sights and 210 places to eat across Osaka — the city of kuidaore, eat till you drop — every one traceable to its source: okonomiyaki teppan, kushikatsu counters, Michelin Bib Gourmand udon and soba, Kita and Minami, the castle, the bay and the Kansai ring.

How this guide was made

How the cuisine filters were policed

Every food card names a specific dish — a label alone doesn’t qualify. A cuisine tag names the kitchen’s own tradition, never one dish it serves. Tabelog and Retty scores may measure popularity but never count as a source.

Web-searched in Japanese and English, fact-checked

Every place is traceable to two credible sources, or a lone Michelin / UNESCO / Agency for Cultural Affairs designation — recorded in data/sources.json. Every coordinate is verified into data/geocodes.json and every place status-checked open. Yelp/TripAdvisor/Tabelog never count toward the two-source bar.
